section: Indian agriculture - importance, land use classification, cropping seasons and cropping pattern
subsections: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings
Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons

accepted.s:
With reference to the Tenth Agriculture Census of India (2015–16), consider the following statements:
1. The total number of operational holdings was about 146 million.
2. The average size of an operational holding was 1.08 hectares.
3. Small and marginal holdings constituted 86.2% of holdings and operated 47.3% of the area.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct for the Tenth Agriculture Census, 2015–16. Small and marginal holdings formed a large majority by number but accounted for less than half of the operated area.
accepted.tq: Use the number-versus-area contrast and verify every figure before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which State had the largest average size of operational holding in the 2015–16 Agriculture Census?
accepted.x: Nagaland recorded the largest average holding size in the 2015–16 Agriculture Census. Ananthapuram and Visakhapatnam are district-level references within Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Separate the all-India State-level fact from the Andhra Pradesh district-level facts.
accepted.sec: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Eleventh Agriculture Census of Andhra Pradesh (2021–22, provisional):
1. The number of holdings increased from 85.24 lakh to 96.90 lakh.
2. The average size of a holding declined from 0.94 hectare to 0.86 hectare.
3. The figures represent provisional State results rather than the standard all-India reference figures.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Andhra Pradesh recorded a rise in the number of holdings and a fall in average holding size in the provisional 2021–22 State results.
accepted.tq: Check whether the statement combines correct figures with the correct geographical and provisional-status qualification.
accepted.sec: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, the largest and smallest average operational holdings, respectively, are found in:
accepted.x: Ananthapuram has the largest average holding in Andhra Pradesh at 1.62 hectares, while Visakhapatnam has the smallest at 0.40 hectare.
accepted.tq: Read the comparison in the order asked: largest first and smallest second.
accepted.sec: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the standard Agriculture Census size classes?
o: Marginal: below 1 ha; Small: 1–3 ha; Semi-medium: 3–5 ha; Medium: 5–10 ha; Large: above 10 ha
Marginal: below 2 ha; Small: 2–4 ha; Semi-medium: 4–6 ha; Medium: 6–10 ha; Large: above 10 ha
Marginal: below 0.5 ha; Small: 0.5–2 ha; Semi-medium: 2–5 ha; Medium: 5–15 ha; Large: above 15 ha
Marginal: below 1 ha; Small: 1–2 ha; Semi-medium: 2–4 ha; Medium: 4–10 ha; Large: 10 ha and above
accepted.x: The standard classes are marginal below 1 hectare, small 1–2 hectares, semi-medium 2–4 hectares, medium 4–10 hectares and large 10 hectares or above.
accepted.tq: Split the options at each boundary, since one altered range makes the entire classification incorrect.
accepted.sec: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Small and marginal farmers, taken together, generally refer to operational holdings of:
accepted.x: Small and marginal farmers together comprise holdings up to 2 hectares: marginal holdings are below 1 hectare and small holdings are 1–2 hectares.
accepted.tq: Combine adjacent size classes rather than selecting the range of only one class.
accepted.sec: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the sowing and harvesting period of Kharif crops?
o: Sown in March–June and harvested in June–July
Sown in October–December and harvested in March–April
Sown in February–March and harvested in August–September
Sown in June–July and harvested in September–October or October–November
accepted.x: Kharif crops are generally sown in June–July with the onset of the south-west monsoon and harvested around September–October or October–November.
accepted.tq: Associate Kharif with the south-west monsoon onset and distinguish it from the short summer Zaid season.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Rabi crops in India are mainly associated with:
o: The onset of the south-west monsoon alone
Only retreating cyclones over the Bay of Bengal
accepted.x: Rabi crops are sown after the monsoon withdrawal and depend substantially on western disturbances and irrigation.
accepted.tq: Identify the climatic and irrigation conditions linked to the season rather than relying only on its calendar months.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:
List-I (Season)
 a. Kharif
 b. Rabi
 c. Zaid
List-II (Representative crop)
 i. Watermelon
 ii. Wheat
 iii. Cotton

 a  b  c
accepted.x: Cotton is a Kharif crop, wheat is a Rabi crop and watermelon is a Zaid crop. Therefore, the correct pairing is a–iii, b–ii and c–i.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure crop-season pairs and eliminate codes containing a mismatched pair.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding the sub-seasons listed in Andhra Pradesh agricultural descriptions is correct?
o: Zaid Kharif is associated with August–September sowing and Zaid Rabi with February–March sowing.
Zaid Kharif is associated with February–March sowing and Zaid Rabi with August–September sowing.
Zaid Kharif is harvested in March–April and Zaid Rabi in October–November.
Both Zaid Kharif and Zaid Rabi are sown only during June–July.
accepted.x: The sub-seasons are described as Zaid Kharif, with August–September sowing, and Zaid Rabi, with February–March sowing.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the two similar labels by matching each with its stated sowing period.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about crop seasons in Andhra Pradesh:
1. Paddy is cultivated in both Kharif and Rabi seasons.
2. The paddy area in 2024–25 was 14.04 lakh hectares in Kharif and 6.93 lakh hectares in Rabi.
3. Rabi paddy has a lower yield than Kharif paddy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Paddy is grown in both seasons, with 14.04 lakh hectares in Kharif and 6.93 lakh hectares in Rabi in 2024–25. Rabi paddy has the higher yield, so statement 3 is false.
accepted.tq: Spot the reversed comparison in the third statement while retaining the correct area figures.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: According to the 2024–25 data for Andhra Pradesh, the total foodgrain area and production were respectively:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 37.51 lakh hectares under foodgrains and production of 161.86 lakh tonnes in 2024–25. The Kharif and Rabi area components were 20.36 and 17.15 lakh hectares respectively.
accepted.tq: Keep area and production units in their proper order and reject options that interchange them.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The foodgrain production of Andhra Pradesh in 2024–25 increased by approximately:
accepted.x: Foodgrain production in Andhra Pradesh in 2024–25 increased by 12.94%. The other figures relate to paddy area or the Kharif and Rabi foodgrain area components.
accepted.tq: Separate the percentage change from the nearby area figures that function as numerical distractors.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following groups consists entirely of food crops?
accepted.x: Food crops comprise cereals, millets and pulses. Cotton, jute, sugarcane, tobacco and several oilseeds are classified as commercial or cash crops.
accepted.tq: Use the classification definition and reject groups made up of commercial or plantation crops.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT classified as a traditional commercial crop of Andhra Pradesh?
accepted.x: The traditional commercial crops listed for Andhra Pradesh are groundnut, cotton, tobacco and sugarcane. Paddy is treated as a food crop.
accepted.tq: Find the single crop belonging to the food-crop group rather than the traditional commercial group.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Groundnut — Oilseed
2. Tea — Plantation crop
3. Fruits — Horticulture
4. Wheat — Commercial crop
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: Groundnut is an oilseed, tea is a plantation crop and fruits belong to horticulture. Wheat is a foodgrain, not a commercial crop, making pair 4 incorrect.
accepted.tq: Identify the wrongly classified item by comparing each crop with its standard group.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following crops is correctly associated with its principal season in the classification given below?
o: Tur or arhar — Rabi; Gram or chana — Kharif
Tur or arhar — Kharif; Gram or chana — Rabi
Both tur and gram — Zaid only
accepted.x: Tur or arhar is identified as a Kharif pulse, whereas gram or chana is identified as a Rabi pulse.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between two commonly confused pulse crops by fixing their seasonal association.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: In Andhra Pradesh, which of the following sets contains only crops reported as being grown in both Kharif and Rabi seasons?
o: Watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, tea and coffee
Tur, gram, tea, coffee and rubber
Cotton, jute, sugarcane, tobacco and tea
Paddy, maize, jowar, bajra and pulses
accepted.x: Paddy, maize, jowar, bajra and pulses are reported as grown in both Kharif and Rabi in Andhra Pradesh. The other groups contain crops associated with a particular season or with commercial and plantation categories.
accepted.tq: Select the complete seasonal set and reject options containing crops outside the stated both-season group.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The yield of Rabi paddy in Andhra Pradesh in 2024–25 was approximately:
accepted.x: Rabi paddy recorded a yield of 6,979 kg per hectare in 2024–25, compared with 5,612 kg per hectare for Kharif paddy.
accepted.tq: Use the direct numerical comparison and distinguish the Rabi value from the lower Kharif value.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Plantation crops — Tea, coffee and rubber
Commercial crops — Cotton, jute and sugarcane
accepted.x: Wheat, rice and pulses are foodgrains. Horticulture includes fruits, vegetables, spices and flowers.
accepted.tq: Find the category whose crop examples have been replaced by a nearby foodgrain group.
accepted.sec: Crop classification - cash vs food crops, crops of both seasons  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following agricultural census references in chronological order:
A. Average Indian holding size was 2.28 hectares
B. Women operated 12.8% of holdings
C. India had an average holding size of 1.08 hectares
D. Andhra Pradesh recorded an average holding size of 0.86 hectare provisionally
accepted.x: The references correspond respectively to 1971, 2010–11, 2015–16 and 2021–22 provisional Andhra Pradesh results. Hence the chronological order is A, B, C, D.
accepted.tq: Anchor the sequence to the census years before comparing the numerical values.
accepted.sec: Agricultural census - size classes, women's share, largest holding state, AP holdings  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A farmer cultivates wheat, barley, gram, mustard and peas after the withdrawal of the south-west monsoon and harvests them mainly in March–April. These crops belong to which season?
accepted.x: Wheat, barley, gram, mustard and peas are Rabi crops. They are generally sown during October–December and harvested during March–April or April–May.
accepted.tq: Infer the season from the sowing, harvesting and crop clues instead of relying on one clue alone.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations contains only crops associated with the Zaid season?
o: Wheat, barley, gram, mustard and linseed
Watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder
Rice, maize, cotton, jute and soybean
Tea, coffee, rubber, cotton and sugarcane
accepted.x: Zaid is the short summer season from March to June, with harvesting generally in June–July. Its representative crops include watermelon, muskmelon, cucumber, vegetables and fodder.
accepted.tq: Recognise the complete Zaid crop cluster and eliminate Kharif, Rabi and plantation crops.
accepted.sec: Cropping seasons - kharif, rabi, zaid  [APPSC]
